raw:
“Thank you.”

Seraphel takes the chair beside yours, folding her wings close so their tips do not brush the table. Her own book is a narrow collection of travel accounts, its cover worn pale at the corners. Professor Stone returns to his papers beneath the magnifying lens.

For several quiet minutes, there is only the turn of pages and the distant uproar from the card table. Someone in the common room says, “That is not a rule,” followed by Dena’s immediate, triumphant “It is now.”

Seraphel glances at the brown volume before you.

“The old records say  
a human seat kept terms clear  
when others preferred fog.”

She opens her book, then looks back to you.

“Did you like copying books,  
or was it only work?”
